symptom: The nightly is green on recent Mendix versions and fails on older ones with `<mapping> now round-trips faithfully — remove it from knownLossy`
cause: `TestMappingFixtureRoundTrip`'s `knownLossy` is a version-blind expectation, but the document it is asserted against is not always version-stable. `loadMappingFixture` uses the **base project's own copy** whenever the blank app already ships a document of that name (FeedbackModule ships two), instead of the pinned `.bson` — and that copy changes with the Mendix version. `FeedbackModule.IMM_PostResponse` loses exactly one property, `MessageDefinition2`, which `modelsdk/gen/mappings/version.go` records as `Introduced: "11.10.0"`, so below 11.10 there is nothing to drop and the staleness guard fires
file: `mdl/executor/mapping_fixture_roundtrip_test.go` (`knownLossyFrom`, and the base-project log line in `loadMappingFixture`)
insight: Gate the entry with `knownLossyFrom` — `ProjectVersion().IsAtLeast(major, minor)` — rather than deleting it, or the real defect (#279) stops being caught on the versions that have it. **Only ONE of the two FeedbackModule mappings failed, and that asymmetry is the diagnosis**: the export twin also loses #277's `IsKey`/`MaxLength` and #279's `MinOccurs`, which exist on every version, so it stays lossy throughout — if both had failed, the cause would have been something else. Check a suspect property against `gen`'s `version.go` `Introduced` before theorising. The substitution that makes this possible is now **logged** ("using the BASE PROJECT's copy"); it was silent, which is what made a one-line cause cost a nightly. To reproduce another version locally: `mxcli setup mxbuild --version 11.6.0` then `MX_BINARY=~/.mxcli/mxbuild/11.6.0/modeler/mx go test -tags integration ./mdl/executor/`. Prove it in both directions — disable the gate and watch the nightly failure reappear on 11.6
